mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4% signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases risk-free discount rates, reducing the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive during the trigger period despite FEDFUNDS > 4%, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3%, the S&P 500 anticipates a faster than expected Fed rate hike path, which compresses growth in equity valuations and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During the trigger period, SPX 20-day returns are positive or the effect is not statistically detectable (p > 0.1) in a 2-year horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) above 200,000 indicates a strong labor market that supports corporate earnings momentum, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 200,000 and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of 0.5% (p > 0.05) during the labor expansion phase.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) grows faster than GDP in the prior quarter, it signals resilient consumer demand that lowers discount rates and boosts S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth rate exceeds GDP quarterly growth rate and is above 2% YoY
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20-day windows where the signal is active (t-test p > 0.05 over 3 years).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly INDPRO (industrial production) index below 105 suggests supply-side softness that reduces market confidence and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 105 and remains below for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During the trigger period, 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.1) or the effect is spurious in a 12-month backtest.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in FEDFUNDS of at least 0.25 percentage points indicate a steady easing cycle that lowers real rates and supports equity valuations, yielding positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS shows 3 consecutive monthly increases each ≥ 0.25%
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20-day windows when the trigger is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, it suggests a tightening labor market that raises wage growth expectations and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 3.5% and remains below for 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the low-unemployment regime (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST (housing starts) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 2021 Q4 averages indicates dual economic strengths that reinforce optimism, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: Both HOUST > 2021Q4_Avg and RSAFS > 2021Q4_Avg for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (F-stat < 4) or 20-day returns are not positive when the joint signal is active (p > 0.05).
